Strongest cross-app alignment in the project — matches Obsidian's own pre-existing binding. ctrl+y in VS Code deliberately displaces Redo (Redo stays on ctrl+shift+z).

F2 is added alongside JetBrains' own inherited Shift+F6 default, not replacing it — both keys must be declared together or Shift+F6 would be lost. VS Code needs no entry, F2 is already its default. Also matches Nautilus's own F2=Rename convention.
Overlaps Nautilus's own ctrl+t = New Tab — accepted deliberately, matches the same convention browsers use.

Confirmed free in both JetBrains and VS Code's own default keymaps, but no native action exists in either editor to select a whole paragraph. Not implemented — nothing to bind yet. Keeping the key reserved here so nothing else claims ctrl+alt+u later.

bindings.action: Select All Occurrences Under Cursor (multi-cursor edit)
bindings.note: VS Code needs no entry — ctrl+shift+l is already its native default (editor.action.selectHighlights) for this exact feature. JetBrains' own default was ctrl+alt+shift+j, moved here for cross-editor consistency. Obsidian has no equivalent command.

Requires the Markdown All in One VS Code extension (yzhang.markdown-all-in-one) — no built-in alternative exists. ctrl+shift+k displaces VS Code's own Delete Line default, which is harmless since Delete Line already lives on ctrl+y in this project. JetBrains keeps ctrl+shift+c alongside the new key rather than losing its native default. See toggle-inline-code-obsidian for the equivalent, pre-existing Obsidian binding (kept on its own separate key, not unified).

No JetBrains action exists for this at all (checked the full bundled Markdown plugin) — dropped there rather than building a custom Live Template. Requires the same Markdown All in One VS Code extension as surround-with-backticks. See insert-codeblock-obsidian for the equivalent, pre-existing Obsidian binding (kept on its own separate key, not unified).

VS Code has no single 'toggle pin' command (a feature request for one is still open upstream) — two conditional bindings simulate it. Moved from Obsidian's previous ctrl+shift+p to alt+p to free that key for Export-PDF in the p3 vault.
The p3 vault previously used ctrl+shift+f for 'show' — unified to ctrl+shift+r to match the other 3 vaults.
Harmless no-op in a vault without the Tasks plugin installed.

Obsidian's own pre-existing binding for the concept behind surround-with-backticks — kept on its own key, not unified with the ctrl+shift+k used elsewhere.

bindings.action: Export to PDF (Obsidian, p3 vault only)
bindings.note: p3-vault-specific habit, not part of the canonical set for the other 3 vaults. Frees ctrl+p for Print. Also requires deleting p3's stale empty overrides on command-palette:open / global-search:open / workspace:close-window so those commands fall back to their real defaults — a manual cleanup step, not something a keybinding entry expresses.

bindings.action: Zoom In / Out (whole-app UI scale, not text size)
bindings.note: VS Code needs no entries — ctrl+plus/ctrl+minus are already its native zoom in/out on every platform. Nautilus already uses the same keys by its own convention. JetBrains' code-folding family (ExpandAll/CollapseAll and the Region variants) had claimed every two-modifier combination on plus/minus, so it's relocated to the three-modifier ctrl+alt+shift+plus/minus (preserving the original numpad-add/subtract secondaries) to free the two-modifier chord for zoom. Reset is deliberately NOT unified — each app keeps its own working default (JetBrains shift+alt+0, VS Code ctrl+numpad0, Obsidian ctrl+0) since forcing one key costs more than a rarely-used action is worth.

Adds ctrl+c/x/v as working shortcuts on macOS alongside the native Cmd+C/X/V, not replacing them (Obsidian entries use the literal Ctrl modifier rather than Mod for exactly this reason). JetBrains needs NO entry at all — $Copy/$Cut/$Paste already inherit control C/X/V from $default with classic secondaries (control INSERT, shift DELETE, shift INSERT); declaring an override here would replace and lose those secondaries for no benefit. VS Code's own ctrl+c/x/v for these commands are gated to non-Mac platforms by VS Code itself, so this only adds real capability on Mac (harmless no-op on Linux, which already has it natively). OPEN QUESTION carried over: Cmd+C/V may not actually work in the JetBrains editor at all under this project's $default-based keymap (a pre-existing characteristic unrelated to this binding) — unverified without a Mac, worth checking for real.
